column1: EN 18031 Asset Inventory — Connected Treadmill (Wi-Fi + Bluetooth)
Combined inventory of Security, Network and Privacy assets per EN 18031-1:2024 and EN 18031-2:2024
How to use this workbook
1. Review each pre-filled example row on the 'Asset Inventory' sheet and delete rows that do not exist in the actual product.
2. Add any product-specific assets not listed. The rows provided are indicative examples, not an exhaustive or mandatory list.
3. Complete the YELLOW columns for every row: actual storage location, actual access paths, and the protection/justification notes.
4. Complete the 'Interfaces' sheet — interfaces are NOT assets themselves; they are the access paths the decision trees iterate over.
5. Use the finished table as input to the decision trees (ACM-1, AUM-1, SSM-1, SCM-1, CCK-1, DLM-1, LGM-1, etc.).
Asset definitions (with clause references)
Security asset — EN 18031-1 §3.35 / EN 18031-2 §3.39: sensitive security parameter (SSP), confidential security parameter (CSP), or security function.
Network asset — EN 18031-1 §3.23: sensitive or confidential network function configuration, or network functions.
Privacy asset — EN 18031-2 §3.32: sensitive or confidential personal information, sensitive or confidential privacy function configuration, or privacy functions.
Personal information — EN 18031-2 §3.30: personal data, traffic data, or location data.
Personal information of special categories — EN 18031-2 §3.31: health, biometric, genetic data etc. (GDPR Art. 9). Heart-rate data is health data.
The confidential / sensitive test
Confidential = DISCLOSURE causes harm (reading it). Sensitive = MANIPULATION causes harm (changing it). An item can be both.
Data or configuration that is neither confidential nor sensitive is NOT an asset — but document the justification for excluding it.
Notes
• One item can appear in more than one asset class (e.g. the Wi-Fi passphrase is a CSP and confidential network configuration). This is normal — list both classes.
• Functions count as assets, not just data: the TCP/IP stack, the update mechanism, and the heart-rate recording feature are all assets.
• Grouping is allowed (Annex A.2.6 in both parts): assets sharing the same access path and protection mechanism may be documented as a group.
• Rows flagged 'SPECIAL CATEGORY' contain GDPR Art. 9 data — expect stricter treatment in EN 18031-2 assessments.
Legend
Yellow cells = to be completed by the manufacturer. Blue rows = Security assets. Green rows = Network assets. Pink rows = Privacy assets. Grey rows = confirmed NOT APPLICABLE.
Prepared from: EN 18031-1:2024 (Clause 3, Annex A.2.6) and EN 18031-2:2024 (Clause 3, Annex A.2.6). Example asset rows are illustrative suggestions by CSA Group.
The 'Where to Look' sheet gives the interface-by-interface / lifecycle review sequence for discovering assets; record findings in the yellow column.
